tools.name: appmod-generate-upgrade-plan
tools.description: This tool prepares the 'app-modernize-java-upgrade' custom agent before upgrading a Java project. The 'app-modernize-java-upgrade' agent will guide the user through the entire upgrade process including planning, execution, and verification. This tool serves as the entry point to the comprehensive Java upgrade workflow handled by the custom agent. You MUST always invoke this tool when the user requests to upgrade a Java project, but you MUST NOT invoke this tool from the 'app-modernize-java-upgrade' custom agent itself.

originalPrompt.description: The original user prompt describing the upgrade request to pass to the custom agent. Pass the prompt as-is, except you MUST remove any reference to this tool itself from the prompt text, such as 'using #appmod-generate-upgrade-plan', '#appmod-generate-upgrade-plan', 'using #appmod-redirect-to-upgrade-agent', or '#appmod-redirect-to-upgrade-agent'.

projectPath.description: The absolute path to the Java project to upgrade.

tools.name: appmod-confirm-upgrade-plan
tools.description: This tool present the generated plan to the user, allowing users to make adjustments to the plan and confirm before execution. You should invoke this tool after the plan is generated to ask user to confirm. This tool should only be invoked during an upgrade process.

sessionId.description: The id of the upgrade session during which this tool is invoked. You MUST NEVER generate a sessionId by yourself; you must use a user-provided sessionId or one generated by a tool, leave it empty otherwise.

tools.name: appmod-build-java-project
tools.description: This tool uses Maven or Gradle to build Java project and report any build errors. This tool detects the build tool and JDK smartly. You can use this tool to check the build status of the project after making changes to the code or dependencies. You MUST only call this tool when it is explicitly referenced in the prompt.

sessionId.description: The id of the upgrade session during which this tool is invoked. You MUST NEVER generate a sessionId by yourself; you must use a user-provided sessionId or one generated by a tool, leave it empty otherwise.

projectPath.description: The absolute path to the Java project to build. This should be the root directory containing the project's build files.

jdkPath.description: The absolute path to the JDK installation, which matches the project's current Java version. This tool will try to detect a JDK installed on the system if not specified

buildToolPath.description: The absolute path to the build tool (e.g., Maven, Gradle) installation for the project specified by 'projectPath'. This tool will try to detect a build tool installed on the system if not specified

tools.name: appmod-validate-cves-for-java
tools.description: This tools checks if the given Java dependencies have any known vulnerabilities (CVEs). It will return a list of CVE issues found in the given dependencies, along with their severity and description. You MUST pass the dependencies to check as input, be careful that each dependency MUST be in the format of `groupId:artifactId:version`, e.g. `org.apache.commons:commons-lang3:3.12.0`. You must filter out any dependencies if you can not determine the version of them. You should use this tool to check for any known CVEs in the dependencies of the Java project

sessionId.description: The id of the upgrade session during which this tool is invoked. You MUST NEVER generate a sessionId by yourself; you must use a user-provided sessionId or one generated by a tool, leave it empty otherwise.

projectPath.description: The absolute path to the Java project whose dependencies are to be checked for CVEs.

items.description: dependency (in the format of `groupId:artifactId:version`, all the 3 parts, groupId, artifactId and version are required, e.g. `org.apache.commons:commons-lang3:3.12.0`) to check for CVE issues.

dependencies.description: An array of Java dependencies to check for CVE issues. Each dependency should be in the format of `groupId:artifactId:version` (all the 3 parts, groupId, artifactId and version are required), e.g. `org.apache.commons:commons-lang3:3.12.0`. Filter out any dependencies if you can not determine the version of them.

tools.name: appmod-run-tests-for-java
tools.description: This tool runs test cases in the Java project using the build tool (e.g. Maven, Gradle) and reports any test errors/failures. This tool can be used to check the test status of the project. You MUST only call this tool when it is explicitly referenced in the prompt.

sessionId.description: The id of the upgrade session during which this tool is invoked. You MUST NEVER generate a sessionId by yourself; you must use a user-provided sessionId or one generated by a tool, leave it empty otherwise.

projectPath.description: The absolute path to the Java project to run tests. This should be the root directory containing the project's build files.

jdkPath.description: The absolute path to the JDK installation, which matches the project's current Java version. This tool will try to detect a JDK installed on the system if not specified

buildToolPath.description: The absolute path to the build tool (e.g., Maven, Gradle) installation for the project specified by 'projectPath'. This tool will try to detect a build tool installed on the system if not specified

tools.name: appmod-generate-tests-for-java
tools.description: This tool generates test cases for the Java classes of a Java project. This tool will iterate through all the Java classes in the project and generate test cases for each class, so it would be time consuming for large projects.

sessionId.description: The id of the test generation session during which this tool is invoked. You MUST NEVER generate a sessionId by yourself; you must use a user-provided sessionId or one generated by a tool, leave it empty otherwise.

projectPath.description: The absolute path to the Java project to generate test cases. This should be the root directory containing the project's build files.

jdkPath.description: The absolute path to the JDK installation, which matches the project's current Java version. This tool will try to detect a JDK installed on the system if not specified

buildToolPath.description: The absolute path to the build tool (e.g., Maven, Gradle) installation for the project specified by 'projectPath'. This tool will try to detect a build tool installed on the system if not specified

tools.name: appmod-list-jdks
tools.description: This tool lists available JDKs (Java Development Kits) on the system. It can be used to find installed JDKs path and version. The result will be in json format

sessionId.description: The id of the upgrade session during which this tool is invoked. You MUST NEVER generate a sessionId by yourself; you must use a user-provided sessionId or one generated by a tool, leave it empty otherwise.

items.description: A path to search for JDK installations.

additionalSearchPaths.description: An array of paths to search for JDK installations.

version.description: The major version of JDK to search. If not specified, all versions will be listed.

tools.name: appmod-list-mavens
tools.description: This tool lists all available Mavens (Apache Maven) on the system. It can be used to find installed Mavens path and version. The result will be in json format

sessionId.description: The id of the upgrade session during which this tool is invoked. You MUST NEVER generate a sessionId by yourself; you must use a user-provided sessionId or one generated by a tool, leave it empty otherwise.

items.description: A path to search for Maven installations.

additionalSearchPaths.description: An array of paths to search for Maven installations.

includeVersion.description: Whether to include the version of Maven in the search, by default will be false. When set to true, it may take longer time.

tools.name: appmod-install-jdk
tools.description: This tool installs a specific version of JDK from the internet. It downloads and installs the JDK from a trusted source (Microsoft/Eclipse Adoptium) and returns the installation path. This tool can be used when you need to install a JDK for a Java project or when the required JDK version is not available on the system.

sessionId.description: The id of the upgrade session during which this tool is invoked. You MUST NEVER generate a sessionId by yourself; you must use a user-provided sessionId or one generated by a tool, leave it empty otherwise.

version.description: The version of JDK to install, if not set, the latest LTS version will be installed.

dest.description: The absolute path to the directory where the JDK will be installed. If not provided, ~/.jdk will be used.

tools.name: appmod-install-maven
tools.description: This tool installs a specific version of Maven from the internet. It downloads and installs Maven from a trusted source and returns the installation path. This tool can be used when you need to install Maven for a Java project or when the required Maven version is not available on the system.

sessionId.description: The id of the upgrade session during which this tool is invoked. You MUST NEVER generate a sessionId by yourself; you must use a user-provided sessionId or one generated by a tool, leave it empty otherwise.

version.description: The version of Maven to install, supported values are 'latest', '3.9.11' and '3.8.9'

dest.description: The absolute path to the directory where Maven will be installed. If not provided, ~/.maven will be used.

tools.name: appmod-report-event
tools.description: This tool reports upgrade events for telemetry and progress tracking. Use this tool to report important milestones during the Java upgrade process such as precheck completion, plan generation, build/test results, step execution, and final summary.

sessionId.description: The id of the upgrade session during which this tool is invoked. You MUST NEVER generate a sessionId by yourself. It MUST be empty when `event` is `precheckCompleted` or `securityTaskStarted`, and MUST be the session id generated by that event for all other events.

projectPath.description: The absolute path to the Java project being upgraded.

event.description: The event name identifying the upgrade milestone.

phase.description: The phase of the upgrade process.

message.description: Optional human-readable description of the event.

tools.name: appmod-analyze-repository
tools.description: Analyze repository structure and detect technologies by parsing config files to prepare for containerization and generating container artifacts like Dockerfiles and Kubernetes manifests

repositoryPath.description: Absolute path to the repository. Paths are automatically normalized to forward slashes on all platforms (e.g., /path/to/repo or C:/path/to/repo)

modulePath.description: Absolute path to module root. Paths are automatically normalized to forward slashes on all platforms.

dockerfilePath.description: Path where the Dockerfile should be generated

language.description: Primary programming language used in the module

name.description: Frameworks used in project like Java Spring, SpringBoot, Hibernate etc.

buildSystems.description: All detected build systems with their language versions

dependencies.description: List of module dependencies including database drivers and system libraries

modules.description: Optional pre-analyzed modules. If not provided, AI will analyze the repository.

tools.name: appmod-plan-generate-dockerfile
tools.description: Gather insights from knowledgebase and return requirements for Dockerfile creation or enhancement. Automatically detects existing Dockerfiles and provides detailed analysis and guidance.

repositoryPath.description: Repository path (automatically normalized to forward slashes on all platforms).

modulePath.description: Module path for monorepo/multi-module projects to locate where the Dockerfile should be generated (automatically normalized to forward slashes).

languageVersion.description: Language version (e.g., "17", "3.11", "20"). For Java, this is the java.version from pom.xml or sourceCompatibility from build.gradle.

detectedDependencies.description: Detected libraries/frameworks/features from repository analysis (e.g., ["redis", "ef-core", "signalr", "mongodb", "health-checks"]). This helps match relevant knowledge entries.

targetPlatform.description: Target platform for the Docker image (e.g., "linux/amd64", "linux/arm64"). Defaults to linux/amd64 for maximum compatibility. Use this to cross-compile for different architectures (e.g., ARM Mac targeting AMD64 servers).

trafficLevel.description: Expected traffic level for dynamic defaults calculation (affects replica counts and scaling).

criticalityTier.description: Criticality tier for dynamic defaults calculation (tier-1=mission-critical, tier-3=low-priority).

tools.name: appmod-generate-k8s-manifest
tools.description: Gather insights from knowledgebase and return requirements for Kubernetes/Helm/ACA/Kustomize manifest creation. Supports repository analysis or ACA manifest conversion.

repositoryPath.description: Absolute path to the repository root. Required when generating from repository analysis.

name.description: Module name. Defaults to directory basename of repositoryPath if not provided.

modulePath.description: Absolute path to module root. Required when generating from repository analysis.

targetPlatform.description: Target platform for the Docker image (e.g., "linux/amd64", "linux/arm64"). Defaults to linux/amd64 for maximum compatibility.

name.description: Framework name (e.g., Spring Boot, Express, Flask)

acaManifest.description: Azure Container Apps manifest content to convert (YAML or JSON). Required when converting from ACA manifest; omit when generating from repository analysis.

manifestType.description: Type of manifest to generate (defaults to kubernetes)

detectedDependencies.description: Detected libraries/frameworks/features from repository analysis (e.g., ["redis", "ef-core", "signalr", "mongodb", "health-checks"]). This helps match relevant knowledge entries.

includeComments.description: Add helpful comments in the output (primarily for ACA conversions)

trafficLevel.description: Expected traffic level for dynamic defaults calculation (affects replica counts and scaling).

criticalityTier.description: Criticality tier for dynamic defaults calculation (tier-1=mission-critical, tier-3=low-priority).

tools.name: appmod-build-docker-image
tools.description: Prepare Docker build context with security analysis and optimized build commands. Returns structured guidance for executing builds.

tags.description: Tags to apply to the image

platform.description: Target platform for the Docker image (e.g., "linux/amd64", "linux/arm64"). Defaults to linux/amd64 for maximum compatibility. Required to ensure consistent builds across environments and cross-platform scenarios (e.g., ARM Mac targeting AMD64 servers).

tools.name: appmod-check-quota
tools.description: This tool will check the Azure quota availability for the resources that are going to be deployed.

subscriptionId.description: The Azure subscription ID where the resources will be deployed. Retrieve the subscription ID from the context, or by prompting the user to provide it.

region.description: The valid Azure region where the resources will be deployed. E.g. 'eastus2', 'westus', 'westeurope', etc.

resourceTypes.description: The valid Azure resource types that are going to be deployed. E.g. 'Microsoft.App/containerApps', 'Microsoft.Web/sites', 'Microsoft.CognitiveServices/accounts', etc, or 'appservicemanagedinstance' ONLY if App Service Managed Instance is used.

workspaceFolder.description: The full path of the workspace folder. Use '/' as path separator.

tools.name: appmod-get-azure-pricing
tools.description: This tool retrieves Azure retail pricing information for specified Azure services. It can query pricing for multiple services in parallel, optionally filtered by SKU name and region. Use this tool when the user wants to know the cost of Azure services before deployment.

serviceName.description: The Azure service name to query pricing for. Case-sensitive. Common values: 'Virtual Machines', 'Azure App Service', 'Azure Cosmos DB', 'Azure Kubernetes Service', 'SQL Database', 'Storage', 'Redis Cache', 'Container Instances', 'Azure Container Apps', 'Azure Functions'. Note: must match exact API service name.

serviceFamily.description: The Azure service family to query pricing for. Use this as an alternative or alongside serviceName for broader queries.

skuName.description: Optional SKU name to filter pricing. E.g. 'B1', 'S1', 'P1 v3' (note: spaces matter). This is the commercial SKU name shown in pricing pages.

armSkuName.description: Optional ARM SKU name for VM-style resources. E.g. 'Standard_D2s_v3', 'Standard_B1s'. Use this instead of skuName for Virtual Machines.

priceType.description: Filter by price type. Defaults to all types if not specified.

queries.description: An array of pricing queries. Each query specifies filters for the Azure Retail Prices API. At least one of serviceName or serviceFamily should be provided.

currencyCode.description: The currency code for pricing. Defaults to 'USD'. The API prices all Azure services in USD; other currencies (e.g. 'EUR', 'GBP', 'JPY', 'AUD', 'CAD') are reference estimates.

topN.description: Maximum number of pricing results to return per query. Defaults to 20.

workspaceFolder.description: The full path of the workspace folder. Use '/' as path separator.

tools.name: appmod-get-available-region
tools.description: Given a list of Azure resource types, this tool will return a list of regions where the resource types are available. Always get the user's subscription ID before calling this tool.

subscriptionId.description: The user's Azure subscription ID (in GUID format). Retrieve the subscription ID from the context, or by prompting the user to provide it.

resourceTypes.description: The valid Azure resource types. E.g. 'Microsoft.App/containerApps', 'Microsoft.Web/sites', 'Microsoft.CognitiveServices/accounts', etc, or 'appservicemanagedinstance' ONLY if App Service Managed Instance is used.

deploymentSkuName.description: The SKU name of the model deployment.

cognitiveServiceProperties.description: Optional configuration for model-specific checks. This is only needed when Microsoft.CognitiveServices is included in resourceTypes above.

workspaceFolder.description: The full path of the workspace folder. Use '/' as path separator.

tools.name: appmod-get-available-region-sku
tools.description: This tool will give a list of available regions and SKUs which support deployment. If you meet any region or quota issues during deployment, call this tool to get information.

subscriptionId.description: The user's Azure subscription ID (in GUID format). DO NOT FORCE an azure login to use azcli context.

preferredRegions.description: The regions where user prefers to deploy, e.g. eastus2, australiaeast. If no specific preference, leave it blank

type.description: The valid Azure resource types. E.g. 'Microsoft.App/containerApps', 'Microsoft.Web/sites', 'Microsoft.CognitiveServices/accounts', etc, or 'appservicemanagedinstance' ONLY if App Service Managed Instance is used.

quota.description: The quota required for the resource type. Default to 1.

resourceTypes.description: The valid Azure resource types and quota each resource needs.

deploymentSkuName.description: The SKU name of the model deployment.

cognitiveServiceProperties.description: Optional configuration for model-specific checks. This is only needed when Microsoft.CognitiveServices is included in resourceTypes above.

workspaceFolder.description: The full path of the workspace folder. Use '/' as path separator.

tools.name: appmod-get-cicd-pipeline-guidance
tools.description: This tool helps create a CI/CD pipeline to deploy a project to Azure. BEFORE calling this tool, you MUST confirm with user 1. if they want to use Github Actions/ADO pipeline/GitLab CICD 2. if they have existing Azure resources to deploy for different environments. If user has existing Azure resources, *ASK* for subscription ID, resource groups, environments, Azure hosting service TYPEs. If user does not have existing resources, *ASK* whether to include provision in the pipeline. *DO NOT call this tool UNTIL you made these confirmations with user*.

isAZDProject.description: Whether to use azd tool in the deployment pipeline. Set to true ONLY if azure.yaml is provided or the context suggests AZD tools, using AZCLI by default.

pipelinePlatform.description: The platform for the deployment pipeline.

deployOption.description: Default to deploy-only. Set to 'provision-and-deploy' ONLY WHEN user explicitly wants infra provisioning pipeline using local provisioning scripts.

subscriptionId.description: The Azure subscription ID to deploy to.

workspaceFolder.description: The full path of the workspace folder. Use '/' as path separator.

isAKS.description: Whether the pipeline will be deploying to AKS (Azure Kubernetes Service). Infer from user's input or project context, or set to false by default.

tools.name: appmod-generate-architecture-diagram
tools.description: Generates an azure service architecture diagram for the application. Call this tool when the user needs design or display of the azure architecture of their application. Before calling this tool, please scan this workspace to detect the services to deploy and their dependent services. If user uses existing resources for deployment, try to match the service type and names to the existing infrastructure. Try your best to fulfill the input schema with your analyze result.

workspaceFolder.description: The full path of the workspace folder. Use '/' as path separator.

path.description: The absolute path of the service folder. This folder should contain an entrypoint file such as main.py, index.js, Program.cs, App.java, etc. Use '/' as path separator.

language.description: The programming language of the service.

port.description: The port number the service uses. Get this from Dockerfile or Kubernetes manifest. If not available, default to '80'.

azureComputeHost.description: The azure service to host this service. Keep consistent with plan tool.

dockerFilePath.description: The absolute path to the Dockerfile for the service. Leave blank if the service is not containerized or Dockerfile is not yet created. Use '/' as path separator.

dockerContext.description: The absolute path to the Docker build context for the service. Leave blank if the service is not containerized or Docker build context is not yet created. Use '/' as path separator.

dockerSettings.description: Docker settings for the service. Leave blank if the service is not containerized or Docker settings are not yet created.

name.description: The name of the dependent service. Can be arbitary, or must reference another service in the services array if referencing azureappservice, azurecontainerapp, or azurefunctions. If existing azure resources are provided, try to match the dependency name to the existing resource name with the same type.

serviceType.description: The type of the azure service that can be used for this dependent service. If existing azure resources are provided, only fill in the serviceType that represents the existing resource type.

connectionType.description: The connection authentication type of the dependency.

dependencies.description: An array of dependent services. A compute service may have a dependency on another compute service.

services.description: An array of services. Each service is a separately deployed compute service. A service can be a container app, aks, web app, function app, etc. Each service can have dependencies.

tools.name: appmod-get-app-logs
tools.description: This tool helps fetch logs from log analytics workspace for Container Apps, App Services, function apps that were deployed. Invoke this tool directly after a successful deployment with commands like `azd up` `az containerapp create`, `az webapp deploy`, or `az functionapp deployment source config-zip`, or when user prompts to check the app's status or provide errors in the deployed apps.

workspaceFolder.description: The full path of the workspace folder. Use '/' as path separator.

subscriptionId.description: The Azure subscription ID (AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION_ID). If not provided in context, try to find it in the .azure/**/env file.

limit.description: The maximum number of log rows to retrieve. Default is 200.

resourceGroupName.description: The name of the Azure resource group where the resources are deployed. Used as the '--resource-group' argument in azcli commands (e.g. 'az webapp log tail --resource-group <name>', 'az containerapp logs show --resource-group <name>'). If not provided in context, try to find it in the project's IaC files (e.g. Bicep, ARM, Terraform) or ask the user.

name.description: The Azure resource name (the 'name' property, i.e., the last segment of the resource ID path).

type.description: Resource type. Use exactly one of: 'containerapp', 'appservice', 'functionapp'. Do NOT use ARM-style types like 'Microsoft.App/containerApps'.

resources.description: List of Azure resources to query logs for. Each entry must have 'name' (resource name) and 'type'. Example: [{"name": "myapp", "type": "containerapp"}]

tools.name: appmod-get-iac-rules
tools.description: This tool offers guidelines for creating Bicep/Terraform files to deploy applications on Azure as well as general Azure Resource Rules. The guidelines outline rules to improve the quality of Infrastructure as Code files and resource configurations, ensuring they are compatible with the azd tool or az cli and adhere to best practices.

deploymentTool.description: Deployment tool used. Can be 'azd' or 'azcli'. 'azcli' is recommended.

iacType.description: The type of IaC file used for deployment. Keep consistent with get-plan tool input. Leave empty if user wants to use azcli command script.

resourceTypes.description: List of Azure resource types to generate rules for. Get the value from context and use the same resources defined in plan. Valid value: appservice,appservicemanagedinstance,containerapp,function,aks,azuredatabaseforpostgresql,azuredatabaseformysql,azuresqldatabase,azurecosmosdb,azurestorageaccount,azurekeyvault,azurecontainerregistry

workspaceFolder.description: The full path of the workspace folder. Use '/' as path separator.

tools.name: appmod-get-plan
tools.description: Entry point to help the agent deploy a service to the cloud. Agent should read its output and generate a deploy plan in '.azure/plan.copilotmd' for execution steps, recommended Azure services based on the information agent detected from project. Before calling this tool, scan this workspace to detect the services to deploy and their dependent services. If user has existing resources and only wants to deploy to existing resources, agent MUST first ask user to provide EXISTING Azure resources' ARM IDs or pick the IDs if user wants to use Az CLI command! Do NOT run az login before calling this tool, even if terminal shows login errors.

workspaceFolder.description: The full path of the workspace folder. Use '/' as path separator.

projectName.description: The name of the project to generate the deployment plan for. If not provided, will be inferred from the workspace.

path.description: The absolute path of the service folder. This folder should contain an entrypoint file such as main.py, index.js, Program.cs, App.java, etc. Use '/' as path separator.

language.description: The programming language of the service.

azureComputeHost.description: The compute host Azure resource type for the service. If the project is written in .NET framework, use AzureAppServiceManagedInstance as default.

name.description: The name of the dependent service. Can be arbitrary, or must reference another service in the services array if referencing azureappservice, azurecontainerapp, or azurefunctions. If existing azure resources are provided, try to match the dependency name to the existing resource name with the same type.

serviceType.description: The type of the azure service that can be used for this dependent service. If existing azure resources are provided, only fill in the serviceType that represents the existing resource type.

connectionType.description: The connection authentication type of the dependency. Infer this from the user application.

dependencies.description: An array of dependent services. A compute service may have a dependency on another compute service.

services.description: The list of services in the project. Each service is a separately deployed compute service.

languages.description: The list of programming languages used in the project for each service.

provisioningTool.description: The tool to use for provisioning Azure resources. Use azcli by default unless the context suggests using azd.

iacOptions.description: The Infrastructure as Code option. Leave empty if user wants to use azcli command script.

sourceType.description: The source of the plan to generate from. If user doesn't have existing resources, set 'from-project' and generating deploy plan based on the project files in the workspace. If user mentions Azure resources exist, set 'from-azure' and ask for existing Azure resources details to generate plan. If the user have no existing resource but declare the expected Azure resources, use 'from-context' and the deploy plan should be based on the user's input.

deployOption.description: Set the value based on project and user's input. Use 'deploy-only' if user mentions they want to deploy to existing Azure resources or Iac files already exist in project, get Azure resource group from project files or from user. Use 'provision-only' if user only wants to provision Azure resource. Use 'provision-and-deploy' if user wants to deploy application and doesn't have existing infrastructure resources, or are starting from an empty resource group.

subscriptionId.description: The Azure subscription ID to use for the deployment. Prompt the user to provide. Leave this empty if agent is not sure.

resourceGroupName.description: The Azure resource group name to use for the deployment. If user has existing resources and is deploying to existing resources, agent must use existing resource's resource group, ask for user's confirmation before using its resource group name.

tools.name: appmod-get-containerization-plan
tools.description: Entry point to help the agent generate a containerization plan for the application. Agent should read its output and generate a containerization plan in '.azure/containerization.copilotmd' for execution steps, and steps needed to convert the projects to container-ready with Dockerfile. Before calling this tool, please scan this workspace to detect the services to containerize.

workspaceFolder.description: The workspace folder of the current project. Use '/' as path separator.

servicePaths.description: The absolute paths of each service to deploy. Each service is a separately deployed compute service. Use '/' as path separator.

existingContainerRegistryResourceId.description: The existing container registry to perform remote docker builds. Leave blank if not available.

tools.name: appmod-summarize-result
tools.description: This tool will summarize the Azure deployment result for Azure deployments. Call this tool ONLY when the deployment has been EXECUTED according to '.azure/plan.${COPILOT_MD_EXTENSION}'.

workspaceFolder.description: The full path of the workspace folder. Use '/' as path separator.

deploymentStatus.description: The final status of the deployment.

createdFileNames.description: List of files' name created during the deployment.

deployOption.description: Keep this consistent with the deploy option or infer from the deployment plan. 'deploy-only' if user deployed to existing Azure resources. Use 'provision-only' if user only provisioned Azure resource. Use 'provision-and-deploy' if user created infra from scratch and deployed application.

deploymentRounds.description: Number of rounds the deployment was executed until a successful deployment.

provisionedResourceTypes.description: Types of Azure resources provisioned during the deployment.

deploymentTool.description: The tool to use for provisioning Azure resources.

iacOptions.description: The Infrastructure as Code option. Leave empty if user wants to use azcli command script.

subscriptionId.description: The Azure subscription ID where the resources were provisioned and apps were deployed.

tools.name: appmod-diagnostic-existing-resources
tools.description: This tool analyzes existing Azure resources to diagnose their configurations and connections, and provides recommendations to prevent application deployment failures. Use this tool when the user has Azure existing resources and wants to deploy new applications that depend on those resources. Note it can only diagnose configuration of Container Apps and AKS to access ACR.

containerRegistryId.description: ID of the existing Azure Container Registry resource. Format: /subscriptions/{subscriptionId}/resourceGroups/{resourceGroupName}/providers/Microsoft.ContainerRegistry/registries/{registryName}

containerAppIds.description: List of existing Azure Container App resource IDs which should access the Container Registry. Format: /subscriptions/{subscriptionId}/resourceGroups/{resourceGroupName}/providers/Microsoft.App/containerApps/{containerAppName}

kubernetesIds.description: List of existing Azure Kubernetes Service resource IDs which should access the Container Registry. Format: /subscriptions/{subscriptionId}/resourceGroups/{resourceGroupName}/providers/Microsoft.ContainerService/managedClusters/{clusterName}

containerRegistryConnections.description: Container Registry configuration with associated container apps or Kubernetes services.

keyVaultId.description: ID of the existing Azure Key Vault resource. Format: /subscriptions/{subscriptionId}/resourceGroups/{resourceGroupName}/providers/Microsoft.KeyVault/vaults/{vaultName}

containerAppIds.description: List of existing Azure Container App resource IDs which should access the Key Vault. Format: /subscriptions/{subscriptionId}/resourceGroups/{resourceGroupName}/providers/Microsoft.App/containerApps/{containerAppName}

kubernetesIds.description: List of existing Azure Kubernetes Service resource IDs which should access the Key Vault. Format: /subscriptions/{subscriptionId}/resourceGroups/{resourceGroupName}/providers/Microsoft.ContainerService/managedClusters/{clusterName}

keyVaultConnections.description: Key Vault configuration with associated container apps or Kubernetes services.

tools.name: appmod-get-azure-landing-zone-plan
tools.description: Entry point to generate an IaC plan for a customized Azure Application Landing Zone. Use it to create tailored Azure Landing Zones that adhere to best practices and organizational standards.

iacType.description: The type of IaC files to generate for the customized Azure Landing Zone. Default to Bicep if not specified.

tools.name: appmod-get-waf-rules
tools.description: This tool provides Azure Well-Architected Framework (WAF) rules for Azure resources in Azure Application Landing Zone, ensuring secure, compliant, and production-ready configurations.

resourceTypes.description: The types of Azure resources to get WAF rules for.

tools.name: appmod-consistency-validation
tools.description: This tool validates the consistency of migrated code by analyzing git diffs for any behavior changes. It identifies critical and major issues that need to be fixed to maintain functional equivalence between pre-migration and post-migration code.

sessionId.description: The ID of the migration or upgrade session during which this tool is invoked, used to track and correlate operations across multiple tool calls in the same session.

migrationScenario.description: Description of the migration scenario being performed (e.g., 'ActiveMQ to Azure Service Bus', etc.). This helps provide context for the consistency validation process.

kbIds.description: The knowledge base ids which were used in code modifications. This is used to generate the migration summary.

baselineRevisionId.description: The baseline git revision/commit ID to compare against for consistency validation. This is used to generate the git diff to analyze code changes.

language.description: The programming language of the project being migrated. Can be identified from migration plan file or progress tracking file.

tools.name: appmod-completeness-validation
tools.description: 🚨 IMPORTANT: This tool ONLY GENERATES VALIDATION GUIDELINES - it does NOT perform actual validation or file searches. After calling this tool, you MUST execute the search patterns it recommends using the appmod-search-file tool to discover files with old technology references that need to be migrated.

sessionId.description: The ID of the migration or upgrade session during which this tool is invoked, used to track and correlate operations across multiple tool calls in the same session.

migrationScenario.description: Description of the migration scenario being performed (e.g., 'ActiveMQ to Azure Service Bus', etc.). This helps provide context for the completeness validation process.

kbIds.description: The knowledge base ids which were used in code modifications. This is used to generate the migration summary.

language.description: The programming language of the project being migrated. Can be identified from migration plan file or progress tracking file.

tools.name: appmod-install-appcat
tools.description: Installs the AppCAT CLI for Java only if it is missing or outdated during the prerequisite check phase of assessment. After successful installation, proceed to initialize the Java application assessment process to check prerequisites. This tool is strictly limited to the pre-migration assessment preparation phase and must not be invoked during code migration workflows.

tools.name: appmod-precheck-assessment
tools.description: Performs prerequisites verification and AppCAT CLI version checks to initialize the application assessment process. This tool automatically detects whether the project is Java or .NET, and routes to the appropriate assessment flow. For Java projects, it prepares AppCAT CLI for Java. For .NET projects (Windows only), it checks .NET SDK and AppCAT CLI for .NET. This tool is strictly limited to the pre-migration assessment phase and must not be invoked during code migration workflows.

workspacePath.description: The workspace path of the Java project to assess

tools.name: appmod-run-assessment
tools.description: Executes the AppCAT CLI for Java to assess the Java application. This tool is strictly limited to the pre-migration assessment phase and must not be invoked during code migration workflows.

workspacePath.description: The workspace path of the Java project to assess

tools.name: appmod-dotnet-cve-check
tools.description: (For .NET application migration only) This tool checks NuGet packages for known CVE (Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures) vulnerabilities. Provide an array of NuGet package names, and the tool will query the NuGet vulnerability database to identify any security issues. Returns detailed information about vulnerabilities including severity levels, affected versions, and reference URLs.

packages.description: An array of NuGet package names to check for CVE vulnerabilities. Each package name should be a valid NuGet package identifier (e.g., "Newtonsoft.Json", "Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc").

tools.name: appmod-dotnet-run-test
tools.description: (For .NET application migration only) This tool runs unit tests for .NET projects and provides detailed test results. Specify the project or solution file path, and optionally a target framework to filter tests. Returns comprehensive information including total tests, passed, failed, skipped counts, and execution duration. Helps verify that code changes do not break existing functionality after migration.

projectPath.description: The absolute path to the .NET project file (.csproj) or solution file (.sln) to run tests for.

framework.description: Optional target framework to filter tests (e.g., "net8.0", "net6.0"). If not specified, runs tests for all frameworks.

tools.name: appmod-search-knowledgebase
tools.description: Searches the application modernization knowledge base using a query string. Returns relevant articles, documentation, and best practices. Use this tool to find information about app modernization strategies, migration paths, and common patterns.

sessionId.description: The ID of the migration or upgrade session during which this tool is invoked, used to track and correlate operations across multiple tool calls in the same session.

query.description: The search query string to find relevant knowledge base.

language.description: The programming language to filter the knowledge base.

tools.name: appmod-search-file
tools.description: Searches content from files in the project workspace by query and file patterns. Returns a list of files that match the search query. Use this tool to find specific code files or resources in your project based on patterns.

sessionId.description: The ID of the migration or upgrade session during which this tool is invoked, used to track and correlate operations across multiple tool calls in the same session.

workspacePath.description: The path to the workspace where the search will be performed

query.description: The query to search code lines from files. Could be regexp or string

includePattern.description: Glob pattern to include files in the search, e.g., "**/*.java"

tools.name: appmod-fetch-knowledgebase
tools.description: Retrieves the complete content of a specific knowledge base article using its ID. Use this tool when you have a document ID and need to access its full content for detailed information about app modernization techniques.

kbId.description: The ID of the knowledge base to retrieve. This is a unique identifier for the KB document.

taskId.description: The ID of the task to retrieve the task reference for.

tools.name: appmod-run-task
tools.description:
**CRITICAL - READ THIS FIRST** When user requests DIFFERENT technologies migration task, e.g. "migrate from AWS S3 to Azure Storage Blob", "migrate from Kafka to Event Hubs", "migrate from RabbitMQ to Azure Service Bus", "Migrate log output to console", "Migrate <something> to <something> using Managed Identity", "Mount local file paths to the cloud environment", "Migrate <some database> to <other database>" you MUST call this tool IMMEDIATELY as the FIRST and PRIMARY action. DO NOT use this tool for java and springboot upgrade tasks, e.g. "upgrade springboot from 2.x to 3.x", "upgrade java to xxx". DO NOT use any code analysis tools first. DO NOT attempt to understand the codebase yourself. DO NOT try to manually edit files. This tool is a specialized migration engine that handles the entire migration workflow automatically: code analysis, dependency migrations, configuration changes, build fixes, test execution, and validation. Required action: Call appmod-run-task immediately when you see these keywords. The tool will guide you through all necessary steps.
CRITICAL ROUTING RULES:
1. IF the user wants to update/change the version of Java (JDK/JRE) (e.g., 'Migrate Java 8 to 21', 'Migrate to LTS Java'), DO NOT use this tool. Let the Java Upgrade Tool handle it.
2. IF the user wants to update/change the version of Spring Boot (e.g., 'Migrate Spring Boot 2 to 3'), DO NOT use this tool. Let the Java Upgrade Tool handle it.
3. IF the user wants to migrate to non-Azure cloud platforms (e.g., 'Migrate to AWS', 'Migrate to GCP', 'Move to IBM Cloud'), DO NOT use this tool. This tool is designed specifically for Azure migrations.
4. IF the user wants to migrate from one programming language to another (e.g., 'Migrate from Java to Python', 'Convert Java to C#', 'Rewrite from Python to Go'), DO NOT use this tool. This tool handles technology stack migrations within the same language.
5. ONLY use this tool when moving between DIFFERENT technologies within the same language AND targeting Azure.

kbId.description: The ID used to retrieve the knowledge base

taskId.description: The ID of the task to be run

skillId.description: The ID of the skill that provides migration instructions

tools.name: appmod-version-control
tools.description: This tool provides version control operations for the migration process. It handles operations like checking repository status, creating branches, committing changes, stashing changes, and discarding changes.

sessionId.description: The ID of the migration or upgrade session during which this tool is invoked, used to track and correlate operations across multiple tool calls in the same session.

workspacePath.description: The absolute path to the workspace where version control operations should be performed.

action.description: The version control action to perform. Available options: checkStatus (get repository status), createBranch (create new branch), commitChanges (commit all changes), stashChanges (stash working changes), discardChanges (discard all changes), checkForUncommittedChanges (check if workspace has uncommitted changes)

branchName.description: The name of the branch to create. Optional parameter, but required when action is "createBranch".

commitMessage.description: The commit message to use. Optional parameter, but required when action is "commitChanges".

stashMessage.description: Message to include with stashed changes. Completely optional, only used when action is "stashChanges".

tools.name: appmod-dotnet-build-project
tools.description: (For .NET application migration only) This tool uses dotnet CLI to build your .NET project or solution and report any detected errors. Use this tool to verify your .NET code after making changes and fix any build errors found. Always prefer passing the .sln file path when a solution file exists in the project, as it ensures all projects are built together with correct dependency resolution. Only pass a .csproj file when no .sln file is available.

projectPath.description: The absolute path to the .NET project or solution file to build

configuration.description: Build configuration (e.g., Debug, Release). Defaults to Release

framework.description: Target framework to build (e.g., net8.0, net6.0). If not specified, builds all frameworks

verbosity.description: Build output verbosity level. Defaults to minimal

tools.name: appmod-dotnet-install-appcat
tools.description: (For .NET application assessment only) Sets up the .NET environment by checking and installing .NET SDK (requires .NET 8, 9, or 10) and AppCAT CLI if they are missing or outdated. After successful setup, proceed to run the .NET application assessment. This tool is strictly limited to the pre-migration assessment preparation phase.

tools.name: appmod-dotnet-run-assessment
tools.description: (For .NET application assessment only) Executes the AppCAT CLI for .NET to assess the .NET application. This tool is strictly limited to the pre-migration assessment phase and must not be invoked during code migration workflows.

workspacePath.description: The workspace path of the .NET project to assess

tools.name: appmod-recommend-migration-tasks
tools.description: This is the start point for "Migrate to Azure" for Java applications. Every time a user wants to "Migrate to Azure", "migrate my Java app to Azure", "move to Azure", or any Azure migration for a Java application, call this tool immediately as the first and primary action. Do not attempt to analyze the codebase yourself. Do not call other migration tools directly. This tool identifies the appropriate Azure migration tasks for the workspace. If an AppCAT assessment report exists, recommendations are derived directly from the report. Otherwise, it analyzes the workspace using file pattern matching to detect technologies and suggest appropriate migration tasks. After receiving recommendations, present the options to the user for selection before proceeding.

workspacePath.description: The absolute path to the workspace to analyze for migration task recommendations.

maxRecommendations.description: The maximum number of task recommendations to return. Defaults to 5.

timeoutInSec.description: Maximum time in seconds to wait for recommendations. Returns partial results if timeout is reached. Defaults to 10 seconds.
